cognitive_validation.rationale: With no candidate novelty present, there is no imaginary scientific or social-organizational system to validate; the story's logic is simply everyday social realism.

novum_candidates.description: Mr. Welles, an indolent aesthete lodger, serves as a device inverting Miss Gould's philanthropic zeal, ultimately dismantling her charitable schemes and reforming her through courtship.
novum_candidates.estrangement_rationale: No reader-facing cognitive estrangement is produced; the contrasts (philanthropist vs. idler, reformer reformed) are those of social satire, not of a science-fictional world-difference. The story presents no alteration of the empirical norm.

narrative_hegemony.rationale: Welles's character and his subversion of Miss Gould's philanthropy do govern the narrative arc, but as a mundane social dynamic, not as an SF novum. Centrality here is to a realist plot, not to any estranging world-difference.

novelty.rationale: This is a realist comedy of manners set in an ordinary New England village. No totalizing or world-altering difference from the empirical norm exists; the situation and characters are mundane social reality with no estranging novum.
